chapter: Dancing schools, Sapiro and Jelly Roll Morton
title: Henri Sapiro, the New Orleans banjoist with a big band
summary: Procope describes Sapiro as a distinguished banjo player who led a big band at the Bamboo Inn.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Well, he was from New Orleans, you know. He was supposed to be a -- what do you call them? A Cajun or whatever, I don't know. We called him Henry Sapiro back then. Henri Sapiro or something like that. He was a banjo player and he told me he played clarinet when he was a little boy. I don't know. A very distinguished looking man. If you saw him you'd think he was I don't know what, you know, dressed very fine, and he had his hair all combed on the side. He was a big fellow and dressed beautiful, fine clothes and he had a band up there at -- and it's a funny thing, I never knew him to have a band anywhere else.
But the Bamboo Inn, yeah. But he had a band, and he had what you call a big band. He had three saxophones, three brass -- four brass, or three or four brass,
